#SUBSECTION 4: Right to Trial, Powers of Lawyers
## Right to Trial
Offenders of Capital Level Violations have the right to invoke a trial to detest the ruling of their capital level violation, should a lawyer be present during a shift and present to represent the offender. Some different types of trials include: - Trial by Debate - This type of trial consists of a short review of the evidence at hand to determine if the ruling was justly placed. The lawyer argues on behalf of the offender(s), and a member of security or command arguing against the offender. A neutral party is needed to act as the judge, typically someone from the command department. The offender's party is permitted to first present up to 3 pieces of evidence that proves the offender's point. The opposing party can then present up to 3 evidence that proves the offender's point false. The neutral party then determines which point is the "correct point". [bold]This type of trial should take no more time than 15 minutes.[/bold] - Instead of the 3 pieces of evidence, either party can choose to call a witness to the violation. Both parties are permitted to call upon the same witness. - A testimony gave by a witness should not take longer than 5 minutes. - Should a testimony be found to have been a lie, the witness is to be charged with Sabotage and either party can request a do-over of the trial occurs. - Trial by Combat - This type of trial consists of a combat being fought by the offender in exchange, should they win said combat, for a reduced sentence. The two options this type of trial presents include: 1. The offender engages in a one on one combat with a member of the crew, as selected by the Captain, Head of Security, or Warden. The terms of said combat are agreed upon by both parties. The lawyer serves as a mediator, assisting in selecting the terms. Some terms include: - Who will be the challenger to the offender? - Should the selected person choose to not participate, a member of command or security is to act in their stead. - Whether or not the duel is to the death or unconciousness. - The weaponry which the duel requires, or a lack of weaponry required. - A determination on if multiple rounds should occur. The maximum amount of permitted rounds for a trial decision is three rounds, overall [bold]being about 15 minutes in total.[/bold] 2. The offender is placed in a space and is made to face, at minimum, 3 different monsters in a sequential order. Should no creatures be available, default to the first option. The lawyer serves as a mediator, assisting in selecting the terms. Some terms include: - How many creatures will the offender be facing? - What weapons or armor may the offender use to combat the creatures? - Will the combat be organized into waves of monsters or a multitude of creatures released at once? - Note: This option takes a lot more time to organize in the moment. As such, it is not recommended. - Trial by Contest - This type of trial consists of a contest between the offender and a member of the crew, as selected by the Captain, Head of Security , or Warden in exchange for a reduced sentence. [bold]This type of trial should take no more time than 15 minutes.[/bold] The lawyer serves as a mediator, assisting in selecting the terms. Some terms include: - What does the contest center upon? - Who is competing in the contest/How many contestants are competing? - If there are multiple rounds, how many will there be? - Alternate Method - If agreed upon by the Captain, Head of Security, or Warden and the offender, an different type of trial can be proposed that does fall within one of these categories. [bold]The duration of any selected trial should be no more than 15 minutes.[/bold]
## Powers of Lawyers
As a lawyer, you are given different legal freedoms to other members of the crew. These powers include: - Restraining Order: You have the legal capability to order an individual to not come within a distance, up to 10 tiles, within another individual. - Caveats: - This restraining order must be specifically requested by the individual who would like someone to stay away from them. - This restraining order must be in writing, and delivered to both parties. - The restraining order must be stamped by the lawyer and signed by the requesting individual. - Restraining orders do not apply during Code Red situations. - The Captain can overturn a restraining order should it prove to be disruptive to the wider crew. - Marriage and Divorce: You have the legal capability to unite two sentient creatures within or seperate two sentient creatures from marriaage. - Caveats: - Both parties must agree to become married, should it be a marriage. - The marriage/divorce papers must be in writing, and delivered to both parties. - The marriage/divorce papers must be stamped by the lawyer and signed by both parties. - Wills: You have the legal capability to establish what is to occur to a sentient creature's assets an self when they die. - Caveats: - The party the will refers to must have requested the will. - The will must be in writing and given to the party. - The will must be stamped by the lawyer and signed by the party. - Lawsuits: You have the legal capability to request assets on behalf of one party wronged by another party. - Caveats: - Both parties must be aware of the lawsuit. - Both parties must recieve documentation of the lawsuit in writing. - The lawsuit must be stamped by the lawyer and signed by the party requesting the lawsuit. - The lawsuit must be stamped by the Warden, Head of Security, Captain, or Head of Personnel to force it into effect. - Cease and Desists: You have the legal capability to request a party cease a certain action on behalf of a wronged party. - Caveats: - Both parties must be aware of the cease and desist. - Both parties must recieve documentation o fthe cease and desist in writing. - The cease and desist must be stamped by the lawyer and signed by the party requesting the cease and desist. - The cease and desist must be stamped by the Warden, Head of Security, Captain or Head of Personnel to force it into effect.
